entities.summary:
Limit is a mathematical concept that represents a value that a function (or sequence) approaches as the argument (or index) approaches some value. This idea has been a cornerstone of calculus for centuries, influencing the development of modern mathematics and science. In the 18th century, mathematicians such as Leonhard Euler and Augustin-Louis Cauchy built upon this concept, laying the foundations for the rigorous study of limits.

The significance of limits lies in their role in defining the behavior of functions and sequences. By examining the limits of functions, mathematicians can gain insights into the properties of functions, such as their continuity and differentiability. This knowledge has far-reaching implications in fields such as physics, engineering, and economics, where understanding the behavior of functions is crucial for modeling real-world phenomena.

The legacy of limits can be seen in the many areas of mathematics and science that have been influenced by this concept. From calculus to number theory, and from physics to economics, limits have played a central role in shaping our understanding of the world. As such, limits continue to be an essential tool for mathematicians and scientists, allowing them to model and analyze complex systems and phenomena.

A striking example of the impact of limits is the work of mathematician and philosopher Bertrand Russell, who famously argued that the concept of infinity is a logical contradiction. This idea, which has been widely debated and refined by mathematicians and philosophers, highlights the importance of limits in understanding the fundamental nature of mathematics and reality.
